text.ms:
1. (1) Kaedah-kaedah ini bolehlah dinamakan Kaedah-Kaedah Buruh

(Lesen Untuk Menggaji Pekerja Bukan Pemastautin) (Sarawak) 2026.

 (2) Kaedah-Kaedah ini mula berkuat kuasa pada 15 Februari 2026.

Tafsiran

2. Dalam Kaedah-Kaedah ini, "pemegang lesen" ertinya orang yang dinamakan

dalam lesen sebagai pemegang lesen.

Permohonan lesen

4. (1) Apabila suatu lesen dikeluarkan, pemegang lesen hendaklah

memastikan—

(a) bahawa pekerja bukan pemastautin itu diambil kerja—

(i) dalam jawatan sebagaimana yang dinyatakan dalam lesen;

dan

(ii) di alamat tempat pekerjaan sebagaimana yang dinyatakan

dalam lesen;

(b) bahawa pekerja bukan pemastautin itu tidak diambil bekerja oleh

mana-mana orang lain selain pemegang lesen;

(c) bahawa dalam hal keadaan kerja telah disiapkan di tempat

pekerjaan yang dinyatakan dalam lesen atau mana-mana tempat

pekerjaan yang dibenarkan oleh Pengarah setelah

mempertimbangkan permohonan untuk mengubah butiran

pekerjaan, Pengarah hendaklah dimaklumkan mengenai status

kontrak perkhidmatan pekerja bukan pemastautin yang terlibat

dalam tempoh tiga puluh hari dari tarikh kerja disiapkan;

(d) bahawa dalam hal penghantaran pulang seseorang pekerja bukan

pemastautin itu ke negara atau Negeri asal, dokumen-dokumen

yang berikut hendaklah dikemukakan kepada Pengarah dalam

tempoh empat belas hari sebelum penghantaran pulang:

(i) satu salinan Memo Periksa Keluar (MPK), jika ada;

(ii) apa-apa dokumen berkaitan daripada Jabatan Imigresen

Malaysia;

(iii) apa-apa dokumen perjalanan termasuk dokumen

penerbangan; atau

(iv) apa-apa dokumen lain yang dikehendaki oleh Pengarah dari

semasa ke semasa;

(e) bahawa tempoh lesen yang dinyatakan dalam lesen itu belum habis

tempoh;

(f) bahawa dalam hal keadaan pemegang lesen itu berhasrat untuk

terus menggaji seorang pekerja bukan pemastautin yang lesennya

akan habis tempoh, pemegang lesen itu bolehlah membuat

permohonan untuk menggaji pekerja bukan pemastautin di bawah

kaedah 3, dalam tempoh enam puluh hari sebelum habis tempoh

lesen itu;

(g) bahawa dalam hal keadaan terdapat apa-apa perubahan kepada

maklumat dalam lesen, pemegang lesen itu hendaklah membuat

permohonan bertulis untuk meminda maklumat itu dalam tempoh

tiga puluh hari dari tarikh pengeluaran lesen kepada Pengarah;

(h) bahawa dalam hal keadaan pekerja bukan pemastautin itu tidak

dapat memasuki Sarawak atas apa jua sebab selepas suatu

permohonan untuk mendapatkan lesen di bawah Kaedah-Kaedah

ini diluluskan, pemegang lesen itu hendaklah memaklumkan

Pengarah secara bertulis dalam tempoh enam bulan selepas

pengeluaran lesen itu;

(i) bahawa lesen yang dikeluarkan di bawah Kaedah-Kaedah ini

hendaklah disediakan untuk pemeriksaan oleh Pengarah

sebagaimana dan apabila dikehendaki; dan

(j) bahawa dalam hal keadaan lesen itu hilang, rosak atau tercemar,

pemegang lesen itu hendaklah serta-merta memohon kepada

Pengarah bagi suatu salinan baharu lesen itu.

LABOUR ORDINANCE OF SARAWAK

LABOUR (LICENCE TO EMPLOY NON-RESIDENT EMPLOYEE) (SARAWAK) RULES 2026

IN exercise of the powers conferred by paragraph 130O(2)(n) of the Labour Ordinance

of Sarawak [Sarawak Cap. 76], the Minister after consultation with the State Authority

makes the following rules:

Citation and commencement

1. (1) These rules may be cited as the Labour (Licence To Employ

Non-Resident Employee) (Sarawak) Rules 2026.

(2) These Rules come into operation on 15 February 2026.

Interpretation

2. In these Rules, "licensee" means the person named in the licence as the holder of

the licence.

Application for licence

3. (1) An application by a person who intends to apply for a licence to employ

a non-resident employee shall be made according to the categories of application for

licence in column (2) and conditions of applications in column (3) of the First Schedule in

writing or by electronic means to the Director by furnishing the following particulars:

(a) name of applicant;

(b) identity card number or passport number of individual applicant, or

registration number if applicable;

(c) address of applicant;

(d) address of place of employment;

(e) name of non-resident employee;

(f) identity card number or passport number of non-resident

employee;

(g) gender of non-resident employee;

(h) designation of non-resident employee;

(i) country or State of origin of non-resident employee;

(j) academic qualifications of the non-resident employee, if academic

requirements are specified; and

(k) working experience of the non-resident employee, if work

experience requirements are specified.

(2) The particulars under subrule (1) shall be furnished to the nearest office of

the Director having administrative jurisdiction for the area in which place of employment

is located.

(3) Upon considering the application for a licence made under subrule (1),

the Director may—

(a) approve the application and issue to the applicant a Licence To

Employ Non-Resident Employee in a form as prescribed in the

Second Schedule; or

(b) refuse the application in writing.

Conditions of licence

4. (1) Upon issuance of the licence, the licensee shall ensure—

(a) that the non-resident employee is employed—

(i) in the designation as specified in the licence; and

(ii) at the address of place of employment as specified in the

licence;

(b) that the non-resident employee is not employed by any other

person other than the licensee;

(c) that in the event work has been completed in the place of

employment specified in the licence or any place of employment

permitted by the Director upon considering the application to

change the particular of employment, the Director shall be informed

of the status of the contract of service of the non-resident employees

affected within thirty days from the date of the completion of work;

(d) that in the case of repatriation of a non-resident employee to his

country or State of origin, the following documents shall be

submitted to the Director within fourteen days prior to repatriation:

(i) a copy of Check Out Memo (COM), if any;

(ii) any related documents from Immigration Department of

Malaysia;

(iii) any travel documents including airline documents; or

(iv) any other documents as required by the Director from time

to time;

(e) that the duration of the licence specified in the licence has not

expired;

(f) that in the event he intends to continue employing

a non-resident employee whose licence will expire, he may make

an application to employ such non-resident employee under rule 3,

within sixty days before the expiry of such licence;

(g) that in the case where there are any changes to the information of

the licence, he shall make an application in writing to amend the

information within thirty days from the date of issuance of the

licence to the Director;

(h) that in the event the non-resident employee is unable to enter

Sarawak for any reason whatsoever after an application for a licence

under these Rules has been approved, he shall notify the Director in

writing within six months after issuance of the licence;

(i) that the licence issued under these Rules shall be made available for

inspection by the Director as and when required; and

(j) that in the event the licence is lost, damaged or defaced, he shall

immediately apply to the Director for a new copy of the licence.
